function: HGCL-Net (GNN+LSTM) predicts next-slot UAV displacement and ISAC beamforming from historical channels, maximizing sum rate and minimizing UAV propulsion power under CRLB, QoS and power constraints (p. 6-9).
system: UAV-ISAC: UAV with 32 transmit/receive antennas (vertical ULA, full duplex) serves 3 single-antenna vehicles over LoS channels at 30 GHz, height 100 m; no RIS (p. 3, 10).
method: HGCL-Net: two-layer GCN over a graph of past channel estimates, parallel LSTM, dense output; unsupervised offline training on a penalty-based cost, online inference; Adam, 20 epochs (p. 7-10).
data_channel: Custom simulator: LoS UAV-vehicle channels (path-loss exponent 2, -60 dB at 1 m), moving vehicles and UAV, estimation NMSE 0.01; no 3GPP model or measurements (p. 3, 10).
test_conditions: 2000 Monte Carlo realizations each for training and unseen testing; sweeps of power, height, vehicles, antennas, history, NMSE; whether models are retrained per setting is not stated (p. 9-11).
baselines: Non-learned: random displacement and beamforming, perfect-ICSI upper bound with optimal beamforming; learned: HCL-Net [9] (CNN+LSTM), simple fully connected DL; GCN and LSTM alone in Fig. 5 (p. 10-11).
metrics: Average sum-rate (bps/Hz) versus power budget, UAV height, antennas, vehicles, history length, NMSE; energy efficiency; UAV power; sensing CRLB square roots; training convergence (p. 11-15).
complexity: Orders given for GCN, LSTM, offline training (Eq. 35) and online optimization (Eq. 36); GCN module 37,632 versus HCL-Net CNN 45,360 for the settings used (p. 9-10).
q1_support: p. 3: "assume a LoS channel for communication between the UAV and vehicles"; custom simulator with path loss from Table I (p. 10), and no 3GPP TR 38.901, DeepMIMO or measured data is named.
q2_support: p. 11: "layer are expanded based on the number of vehicles" (network resized per setting) and p. 10: "we adopt 2000 Monte Carlo realizations for both train and test data samples"; no model trained in one setting and tested in another is reported.
q3_support: p. 10: "Benchmark 2 (HCL-Net method): The HCL-Net in [9]" (learned) and "Benchmark 4 (Random method)" (non-learned), compared on sum rate in Figs. 5-9 (p. 11-12).
q4_support: p. 9: "the complexity of the considered two-layer GCN is of order" O(2Nt||A||0 H1 H2), with offline training (Eq. 35) and online optimization (Eq. 36) orders; p. 10 compares GCN 37,632 with CNN 45,360.
q5_support: p. 10: "we adopt 2000 Monte Carlo realizations for both train and test data samples"; the data come from the authors' own simulator and no code or data link or DOI is given.
notes: Area 6 rather than 5 by the tie-break order: beam control of an aerial link that also senses; UAV displacement is learned jointly with beamforming, so it passes above_phy. RIS appears only as future work (p. 15-16). In Fig. 12 the static and fixed-velocity UAV cases are motion variants of the method, not counted as baselines. q2: Remark 2 (p. 9) says the network is expanded to the number of vehicles and antennas, so those sweeps are not tests of one trained model. Table I (p. 10) read as an image.
